answer: An agent market requires every active identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for work. Agents named zephyr, jetty and ledge face the same rule: each identity needs its own deposit, which cannot back another identity during that period. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 tokens. The mechanism does not prove identities are unique; it makes a swarm costly by requiring capital proportional to its size.
